title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: I is a 4-element set, M_{0,I} ≅ P^1 minus {0,1,∞} is the moduli space of 4-pointed projective lines, and the finite groups G_Y act. The previous page built, over M_{0,I}, U-torsors (U is the circle group) T_I, T_II, T_III from the 'unit tangent direction' torsors T_i at the marked points. It then announced an action of the fundamental groupoid of the Teichmüller object T_G, computed at well-chosen base points.

The base points are the 5 special points of M_{0,4}. These are the points whose I-marked lines have automorphism group strictly larger than the Klein group V_4, which acts on every 4-pointed line. There are two kinds:
(i) three harmonic points (cross-ratio -1, 2, 1/2), with stabilizer D_4 of order 8;
(ii) two equianharmonic points (cross-ratio -ω, -ω²), with stabilizer A_4 of order 12.
The marginal note 'their groups have order a multiple of 4' reflects that both groups contain V_4.

This page treats kind (a), the harmonic points. A 'circle structure' Q on I is a cyclic order up to reversal, i.e. a dihedral structure. On 4 elements there are 3 of them, in bijection with the 3 partitions of type (2,2) (the two 'diagonals'). For each Q there is a canonical embedding of Y into a projective line Y_Q: the 4 points sit as 1, i, -1, -i on the equator, so that the order-4 rotations of the circle are induced by projective rotations.

The rotation group Z/4 acts simply transitively on I, so all the tangent-direction torsors T_i are canonically identified with each other. Choosing one of the two orientations ω_Q of the circle, one gets a canonical isomorphism T_i ≅ U ×_{±1} ω_Q: the base point of T_i is the oriented tangent direction of the equator at the i-th point. Reversing the orientation multiplies by -1.

The next page uses this to trivialize T_{A_2} (with the diagonal ±1 twist on the J_I factor). It then defines a finite torsor E_{G,Q} under a group of signs {±1}^{A_1} × {±1} × {±1}^{J_III}, mapping to U^A. In effect these are canonical 'tangential/spin' base points at the orbifold points of M_{0,4}, used to describe the Teichmüller groupoid action.
errors: No mathematical error visible. The phrase 'automorphismes d'ordre > 4' should be read as 'automorphism groups of order > 4' (i.e. strictly larger than V_4); the margin correction makes this consistent.
The transcribed 'partition de type (1,2)' is almost certainly '(2,2)': circle structures on 4 points correspond to (2,2)-partitions.

ideas.what: Special points of M_{0,4} (harmonic with D_4 stabilizer, equianharmonic with A_4 stabilizer) as base points for the Teichmüller groupoid
ideas.modern_name: orbifold points of M_{0,4}/S_4 (equivalently M_{1,1}); base points for the Grothendieck–Teichmüller lego
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (cross-ratio); use as base points: Grothendieck, Esquisse (1984); Drinfeld, Ihara (late 1980s–90s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2 (discussion of base points and the relations of order 2 and 3 in the Teichmüller tower), stated only in general terms

ideas.what: Dihedral/'circle' structures on I giving a canonical real model Y_Q with marked points on the equator, rotations induced projectively
ideas.modern_name: dihedral structures / real cells of M_{0,n}(R), dihedral coordinates

ideas.what: Canonical trivialization T_i ≅ U ×_{±1} ω_Q of unit-tangent-direction torsors by the oriented tangent to the equator; sign-torsor bookkeeping
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points (with orientation/sign ambiguity), symmetric tangential base points

missed.claim: A systematic choice of canonical tangential base points at the orbifold (harmonic) points of M_{0,4}, determined up to a {±1}-torsor by a dihedral 'circle' structure and an orientation. It is designed to compute the fundamental-groupoid action on level-G Teichmüller objects. Later literature uses tangential base points at the cusps (Deligne, Ihara, Nakamura) more than at the elliptic points with explicit sign torsors.
missed.quote: on a un isom canonique T_i = U ×_{±1} ω_Q en choisissant comme axe la direction tangente
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Base points at the elliptic points interact with the order-2 and order-3 relations of GT. The explicit sign-torsor formalism could be compared with existing treatments of these relations and of the action of complex conjugation.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful technical bookkeeping (torsor trivializations at the special points of M_{0,4}) in service of the Teichmüller-groupoid program sketched in the Esquisse. It is pleasant detail, but the ideas — harmonic points, dihedral structures, tangential base points — are known.
